blocks.text: Your body contains T cells able to recognise essentially any peptide, yet the genome has only about twenty thousand genes. The solution is that each T cell builds its own receptor by cutting and joining gene segments, and then the thymus tests every new receptor before the cell is allowed to leave.

blocks.markdown: T cell precursors arise in the bone marrow and travel to the **thymus**, where they mature. A mature T cell carries a unique **T cell receptor (TCR)**, which must (1) recognise peptide displayed on **self MHC** and (2) not react strongly to self peptide. The thymus enforces both requirements.

**The TCR.** Most T cells carry an **αβ TCR**, a heterodimer of an α and a β chain, each with a variable (V) and constant (C) domain. The variable domains contain three hypervariable loops (CDR1 to CDR3) that contact the peptide-MHC complex; CDR3 is the most diverse. The TCR is associated with the **CD3** complex, whose cytoplasmic **ITAM** motifs signal when the TCR is engaged. A minority of T cells carry a γδ TCR. Unlike antibodies, TCRs recognise only peptide-MHC and are never secreted.

**Somatic recombination.** The TCR genes exist as separate gene segments: the β chain locus has **V, D and J** segments plus constant genes; the α chain locus has **V and J** segments. In each developing T cell, the enzymes **RAG1 and RAG2** (recombination-activating genes) cut the DNA and join one V, one D and one J segment (β chain) or one V and one J segment (α chain). Further diversity comes from **junctional diversity**: nucleotides are removed by exonuclease and random nucleotides are added by **terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase (TdT)** at the joins. Finally, any α chain can pair with any β chain. Together these processes produce an enormous repertoire, far more diverse than could be encoded by individual genes.

blocks.caption: Combinatorial diversity for a chain with V, D and J segments (the α chain lacks D)

blocks.title: Counting combinations
blocks.prompt: In a simplified model, the β chain has 30 V, 2 D and 10 J segments and the α chain has 40 V and 50 J segments. Estimate the combinatorial diversity of the αβ TCR, ignoring junctional diversity.

steps.text: Pairing of any α with any β.
Interpret: even this simple model gives over a million receptors; junctional diversity multiplies this many times. Numbers are for illustration; real loci have somewhat different segment numbers.

blocks.answer: About 1.2 × 10^6 combinations from segment choice alone.

blocks.markdown: **Thymic development.** Progenitors enter the thymic cortex lacking CD4 and CD8 (**double negative**). They rearrange the β chain; a successful β chain pairs with a surrogate chain (pre-TCR) and signals survival and proliferation. The cell then expresses both **CD4 and CD8 (double positive)** and rearranges the α chain. Double-positive cells are then tested.

blocks.caption: Thymic selection

blocks.title: Where does this cell die?
blocks.prompt: Three double-positive thymocytes are tested. Cell A cannot bind any self MHC. Cell B binds self MHC class II with moderate affinity. Cell C binds a self peptide on MHC class I extremely strongly. Predict the fate of each.

steps.text: Cell A: it fails positive selection because it cannot recognise self MHC. It dies by neglect in the cortex.
Cell B: moderate affinity for class II passes positive selection; it commits to the CD4⁺ lineage (CD8 lost) and goes on to the medulla.
Cell C: it binds class I, so would be CD8-lineage, but binding self peptide extremely strongly means it will be removed by negative selection (apoptosis).
Summary: only cells that recognise self MHC weakly, and self peptide not too strongly, leave the thymus.

blocks.answer: A dies by neglect, B becomes a CD4⁺ T cell, C is deleted by negative selection.

blocks.markdown: **CD4 and CD8 co-receptors.** CD4 binds a non-polymorphic region (β2 domain) of MHC class II; CD8 binds the α3 domain of MHC class I. They have two functions: they **stabilise** the TCR-peptide-MHC interaction, and they carry the tyrosine kinase **Lck** on their cytoplasmic tails, which phosphorylates the CD3 ITAMs to start intracellular signalling. They also determine which cells a T cell can respond to: CD4⁺ T cells respond to MHC class II (professional APCs, helper function), CD8⁺ T cells to MHC class I (any nucleated cell, cytotoxic function).

blocks.title: Selection links the receptor to the co-receptor
blocks.text: The class of MHC that a TCR recognises during positive selection decides whether the cell keeps CD4 or CD8. This matching ensures that helper cells are restricted to class II and cytotoxic cells to class I.

points: Positive selection in the cortex keeps T cells whose TCR recognises self MHC; negative selection removes those binding self strongly.
TCR diversity arises from RAG-mediated V(D)J recombination, junctional diversity (TdT) and α-β pairing.
CD4 binds MHC class II and CD8 binds MHC class I, stabilising the TCR and recruiting Lck.

questions.stem: What is the fate of a double-positive thymocyte whose TCR cannot bind any self MHC molecule?

options.text: Conversion to a regulatory T cell

distractorRationale.a: Positive selection requires binding self MHC.
distractorRationale.b: Negative selection eliminates strongly self-reactive cells.
distractorRationale.c: Correct: failure of positive selection leads to apoptosis (death by neglect).
distractorRationale.d: Treg diversion applies to cells with high self-affinity.

questions.explanation: Positive selection tests for recognition of self MHC. A thymocyte that fails to bind receives no survival signal and dies by neglect, the fate of most thymocytes.

questions.stem: Which thymic cells mediate positive selection?

distractorRationale.a: Correct: cortical epithelial cells present self peptide-MHC for positive selection.

questions.explanation: Cortical thymic epithelial cells express MHC class I and II with self peptides and provide the survival signals for positive selection.

questions.stem: Which enzymes are essential for cutting DNA during V(D)J recombination?

distractorRationale.a: Correct: RAG1/RAG2 initiate recombination in developing lymphocytes.
distractorRationale.b: AID mediates hypermutation and class switching in B cells.
distractorRationale.c: Perforin and granzyme are CTL cytotoxic proteins.
distractorRationale.d: NADPH oxidase is used in phagocyte killing.

questions.explanation: RAG1 and RAG2 recognise recombination signal sequences and cut DNA. Their absence blocks T and B cell development.

questions.stem: Which process adds random nucleotides at the junctions between gene segments, increasing TCR diversity?

distractorRationale.b: Class switching is a B cell process involving heavy-chain constant region.
distractorRationale.c: Complement does not modify receptor genes.
distractorRationale.d: AID acts in B cell mutation and switching.

questions.explanation: TdT adds non-templated (N) nucleotides at junctions, contributing to junctional diversity concentrated in CDR3.

questions.stem: A mature T cell has a TCR that recognises a peptide presented by HLA-DR and expresses CD4. What is the role of CD4?

options.text: It binds the MHC class II β2 domain and recruits Lck, stabilising the interaction

questions.correctOptionText: It binds the MHC class II β2 domain and recruits Lck, stabilising the interaction

distractorRationale.a: Correct: CD4 binds class II and brings Lck close to the TCR-CD3 complex.
distractorRationale.d: CDRs of the TCR form the binding site.

questions.explanation: CD4 enhances signalling by binding class II and bringing Lck to phosphorylate CD3 ITAMs. It does not recognise peptide.

questions.stem: True or false: CD8 binds MHC class I and is expressed by T cells that recognise MHC class I-peptide complexes.
questions.explanation: CD8 binds the non-polymorphic α3 domain of MHC class I, and CD8⁺ T cells are class I-restricted (cytotoxic). Co-receptor choice is set during thymic selection.

questions.stem: A simplified TCR β chain locus has 45 V, 2 D and 13 J segments. How many different β chains can be made from segment choice alone?
questions.explanation: The number is 45 × 2 × 13 = 1170. Junctional diversity then multiplies the repertoire further.

questions.stem: For an α chain with 50 V and 60 J segments and a β chain with 40 V, 2 D and 12 J segments, how many αβ combinations are possible from segment choice and α-β pairing alone? Give your answer in units of 10^6.
questions.explanation: α: 50 × 60 = 3000. β: 40 × 2 × 12 = 960. Pairing gives 3000 × 960 = 2,880,000 = 2.88 × 10^6. These are model segment numbers for illustration and do not include junctional diversity.

questions.stem: Describe positive and negative selection in the thymus and the fate of cells in each.
markingGuide: Positive selection in cortex: TCR must recognise self MHC with weak affinity; failure: death by neglect
Lineage commitment: class I gives CD8, class II gives CD4
Negative selection in medulla: strong binding to self peptide-MHC causes apoptosis (or Treg diversion)
questions.explanation: Selection yields T cells that are useful (MHC-restricted) and safe (not strongly self-reactive).

questions.stem: Explain how somatic recombination generates T cell receptor diversity.
markingGuide: Gene segments V, D, J (β) and V, J (α) recombined by RAG1/RAG2
Combinatorial diversity from the choice of segments
Junctional diversity: exonuclease trimming and TdT N-nucleotide addition
Pairing of α and β chains
Result: large repertoire, with CDR3 most variable
questions.explanation: Diversity comes from rearrangement at the DNA level in each developing T cell, not from inheriting a different gene for every receptor.
